Strengths: Finally, Norway/IMDI welcomes WHO's leadership in developing this guidance. The document has the potential to become an important global reference for countries seeking to establish sustainable, interoperable, and scalable digital health ecosystems. Its alignment with broader health system strengthening objectives provides a valuable basis for supporting Universal Health Coverage, Health for All, and the Sustainable Development Goals.

Norway/IMDI has extensive experience in the development and implementation of digital solutions and recognises well the presented considerations supporting of a common digital architecture for health. The document successfully articulates the unique requirements of the health sector and demonstrates why health information systems require specific governance, interoperability, security, and architectural considerations, as well as emerging topics such as artificial intelligence and the importance of high-quality data as prerequisites for future innovation.

While the document is comprehensive, it is also extensive and complex. Norway appreciates the inclusion of reading guidance, summary illustrations, and overview figures, which significantly enhance accessibility and help readers navigate the content.
